Morphine, codeine and methadone are all opioid analgesics.

**Morphine**:

Naturally occurring opiate.

Metabolised predominantly in liver through glucuronidation by UGT2B7 to:

- Morphine 3 glucuronide (70%) inactive
- Morphine 6 glucuronide (10%), active metabolite and 13x more potent then morphine. 
- It may also be metabolised to codeine and normorphine 

**Codeine**:

Codeine is an opiate with minimal intrinsic activity, its predominant analgesic effect is from it metabolism to morphine. 

Its undergoes 

- Glucuronidation to codeine-6­ glucuronide (70%)
- Metabolised hepatically by CYP2D6  to active morphine (10%) → Glucuronidation M3G and M6G (active)
- Metabolised hepatically by CYP3A4  to norcodeine (10%) not active 

Importantly the CYP2D6 metabolism demonstrates significant genetic polymorphism with people being 

- poor metabolisers  \~10% Caucasian population and 30% Hong Kong Chinese 
- intermediate metabolisers \~10% Caucasian population up to 50% Asians 
- extensive metabolisers (normal) \~80% Caucasian population
- rapid metabolisers 1-2% Caucasian population and Asian, 20-30% of Saudi and North African 

Poor metabolisers with have limited analgesic effects from codeine while rapid metabolisers may have excess effect and subsequent side effects.

**Pethidine**

Pethidine is a synthetic opioid.

Undergoes hepatic metabolism to norpethadine

Norpethidine has 50% potency of pethidine and Neuro-excitatory properties including seizures and hallucinations  

may accumulate in renal failure
